messages:
mae-support: Hey team, escalating a private/VPC connectivity issue from customer Eve. Their app can't reach our hosted inference endpoint from a peered VPC — TLS handshake fails intermittently, only from that peered subnet. They see ECONNRESET and TLS alert: handshake_failure in app logs. Ticket #INC-8421. Can network folks triage?

Eve-customer: Repro steps I ran: curl to endpoint times out or returns early TLS error. From other subnets in same account it's fine. We only see failures when traffic goes through a transit VPC with a security appliance.

raj-netops: Thanks — can you paste the curl/openssl output and a tcpdump (first 100pkts) from the host when the failure happens? Also confirm whether the transit VPC has NACLs vs. stateful SGs + an inline WAF.

Eve-customer: short outputs attached in ticket, paste here small excerpts: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect inference.redwood.ai:443 -servername inference.redwood.ai -brief
CONNECTED(00000003)
139832...:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:SSL3_GET_RECORD:wrong version number:../../ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:???
```

mae-support: They say transit VPC uses a managed WAF appliance and has stateless NACLs on the subnet with some custom deny rules. Might be a rule ordering issue.

sam-eng: Quick checklist — usually causes: asymmetric NAT (reply path not back through same appliance), NACL deny rule shadowing ephemeral port replies, or TLS interception (SNI rewrite / cert replacement) by the appliance. If they see wrong version number, likely middlebox touching TLS.

raj-netops: Agreed. Two immediate things to check: 1) NACL rule ordering for the transit subnet — a broad DENY could match ephemeral source ports and drop responses. 2) IP translation: ensure SNAT/EIP on NAT gateway isn't causing replies to go direct to customer app bypassing appliance.

mae-support: Eve — can you run these from the app host and paste results?
1) curl with verbose to capture TLS handshake:
```
curl -v --tlsv1.2 https://inference.redwood.ai/health
```
2) openssl s_client with -msg and tcpdump on port 443:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -n -s 0 port 443 and host inference.redwood.ai -w /tmp/trace.pcap
openssl s_client -connect inference.redwood.ai:443 -servername inference.redwood.ai -msg
```

Eve-customer: Ran tcpdump, attaching pcap link in ticket. Quick grep shows a lot of RST after ClientHello the times it fails.

raj-netops: Can you upload a short tcpdump ascii of the handshake? Example filter output we want: timestamps, srcIP:srcPort -> dstIP:443 flags, and TLS alert if present. Also paste the NACL rules (order + rule numbers) for the transit subnet.

Eve-customer: NACL excerpt:
```
100 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 80-80
110 DENY 10.0.0.0/8 TCP 32768-61000
120 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 ALL 0-65535
```

sam-eng: Bingo — rule 110 denies a broad ephemeral port range for destination in 10.0.0.0/8; that can drop the server -> client response traffic if the server's reply uses a high source port or if translation changes source/dest. Order matters — DENY before wide ALLOW will shadow it.

raj-netops: Exactly — NACLs evaluate by rule number; lower number first. Their DENY is evaluated earlier. Because it's stateless, return traffic needs matching allow on ephemeral ports too. In this case the DENY blocks the server's reply or NATed responses.

mae-support: Recommended temporary mitigations for customer: 1) Move DENY rule to higher number (after the wide allow) or narrow its CIDR/ports. 2) Add explicit ALLOW for source/destination ephemeral range for the affected CIDRs. 3) Bypass TLS-inspecting WAF for this destination if it's doing SNI rewrite.

sam-eng: Example NACL fix: change rule 110 to a higher rule number (e.g., 190) or replace with:
```
110 DENY 10.0.0.0/8 TCP 22-22    # keep ssh deny
120 ALLOW 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 32768-65535
```
Or even better, restrict the deny to the exact internal CIDR of concern rather than 10.0.0.0/8.

Eve-customer: We changed the NACL to allow ephemeral ports and retested — TLS handshake now succeeds consistently. Thank you.

mae-support: Great. Can you confirm whether the WAF was also rewriting certs? If not, we'll close the ticket.

Eve-customer: WAF was only logging but not in-path for this flow. Looks like NACL ordering was root cause. Closing on our side, will leave ticket notes. :thumbsup:

raj-netops: Filing internal blameless note — remind customers that stateless NACLs need symmetric rules for ephemeral ports. I'll add a short KB on this. :memo:

deploy-bot: New note added to ticket INC-8421 by raj-netops: "NACL rule ordering blocked inference replies; customer fixed by allowing ephemeral ports. Recommend KB + onboarding checklist."

mae-support: Thanks everyone, marking as resolved unless Eve reports further issues. :white_check_mark:
